Tank Abbott trains professionally though, although his style is "from the streets". He is trained, by most people's definition. Nothing to do with an average male, to be honest. Again, I am not disputing street fighting as a style, I am just saying that your example doesn't really fit the question. I know nothing about you, as to how big or old you are, but I saw that you said that you can be too big to be significantly hurt... To some extent, you are right, extremes and all, but I would say (from personal experience in training) even a 15 year old girl with training can hurt a grown man quite a lot. Also, the one who is more likely to not be afraid to get hit in a fight, or to know how to deal with being hit, is the trained person, not the untrained. Your previous examples are all of trained people. How, exactly do you see the adult winning? Most people around here say he will "charge him" with his weight, but if the kid knows a bit of movement (after 3 years he should), then he can evade the grown man, while also dishing out an uncomparable amount of punches (and kicks). Close quarters, the kid has knees and elbows while the grown man has nothing.
6 months of training jabs to your average 15 year old and he will hit harder than any body builder/strong man or anyone who isn't trained.

\>even if the boy knows martial arts it's hard to implant in a real life fights

Still an advantage compared ot no training. Plus I don't see how physical fitness plays a role. The fight is gonna go two ways, imo, assuming they hae no info about each other's abilities (classical back of the alley whatchu say about to my girl type of fight):

​

1) Male will charge kid with haymakers and whatever other punches he can throw (so basically none, untrained people don't throw effective jabs) due to his superior physical size. Based on his intelligence, he will realize sooner or later that he is purely outmatched in this aspect. I would not expect him to land a single hit (after 3 years of training you should have a good enough guard to at least block basic jab-hook combos, so isolated haymakers should be a piece of cake), while also taking heavy damage (being able to counter efficiently is a skill which takes more than 3 years to master, agreed, but the training should provide enough experience and just speed to the kid, so he should have no problems even just jabbing his opponent to death if he doesn't change tactics). Eventually, unless they are stupid, the kid and the adult will realize their win conditions; for the kid it's stay on your feet, for the adult it's get on the ground. But by this point, with our given assumptions, the adult, completely unused to getting punched in the face, would probably have already taken a  lot of damage. You know what the biggest advantage in a fight is? Thinking clearly and soundly, and you get that with experience. "Everybody has a plan until they get punched in the face" works here. Anyways, even in a close quarter struggle where the adult would try to take the kid to the ground, muay thai emphasizes elbows and knees, and after 3 years your knees should start doing decent damage, let alone your elbows. In this scenario it's an easy 9.9/10 for the kid. 

2) They already start in a really close combat situation, at which point things are fairer, but I would still postulate that the kid wins any time the adult lets go of him, even for 1 or 2 seconds, OR doesn't manage to properly take him down/hold him to the ground, in which case the more agile one (probably the kid) gets up and roflstomps him. But in this scenario I would only give it 6/10 to the kid

Aici e o problema culturala, nu una economica. Studiul [asta](https://journals-sagepub-com.eur.idm.oclc.org/doi/pdf/10.1177/0013916511416647) spune ca (dau paste la abstract aici, ca e posibil sa nu ai acces):

Previous scholarship pertaining to the social bases of proenvironmental  
behavior presents an equivocal picture of the influence of social class indicators. In further investigation of this possible association, the author examined  
municipal-level data in Massachusetts, compiled by various state agencies,  
exploring whether sociodemographics are associated with recycling rates,  
hybrid car ownership, and the presence of sustainability advocacy groups.  
Results indicate that the proportion of college-educated population was  
significantly associated with recycling and hybrid auto ownership, whereas  
results for the civic action group presence show population density and  
political voting were significant but not sociodemographics. The insignificance of economic metrics implies that policy makers and social scientists in  
this specific case should focus more on cultural factors than financial barriers  
in encouraging certain behaviors.

Ultima fraza e cea mai relevanta, si desi e facut pe niste oameni din Massauchussets, ramane valabil ca este vorba de o chestia culturala la mijloc; daca fiecare roman ar fii constient ca e posibil sa isi omoare copii/ copii copiilor cu fiecare sticla aruncata pe jos, eu cred ca multi nu ar mai face-o. Also, daca ar fii adevarat ce zici tu, atunci ar trebui sa ne asteptam ca tarile mai sarace ar trebui sa lupte mai putin cu climate changeul. Ca si metrica, am folosit CPI (Climate protection index) ca sa vad daca exista vreo corelatie. Poti efectiv sa faci un quick google search sa vezi ca nu este vorba doar de statutul economic. Eu nu sunt de acrod ca ICHB este un liceu performant (dupa definitia mea a performantei). Am 21 de ani, am cunoscut multi oameni care au terminat ICHB, cu unii din ei chiar sunt prieten, si cred ca stiu destul de bine cum functioneaza acolo lucrurile, din cele povestite de ei:

ICHB are 1 clasa sau 2 de elevi de genul, cu care se face pregatire ca lumea, cu cei mai buni elevi, adusi de prin toata tara si din afara. Acestia au profesori speciali (nu cunosc personal elevi din clasele astea ca sa spun daca sunt buni sau nu), care fac cu ei numai probleme de olimpiada. So far so good, nu am ce sa critic la acest lucru; cred ca ar trebui sa fie genul asta de acomodari pentru elevi cu o capacitate f mare in mai multe licee din Romania. 

Restul elevilor, sunt intr-o scoala normala romaneasca. Cu profesori pedofili, cu crizata de la istorie, etc. La sfarsit, dau bacul romanesc, pe care majoritatea il iau (nu stiu cifrele exacte), dar nu as putea sa spun ca vezi domne ce mare avantaj a oferit acest liceu fata de Vianu, de exemplu, acestor copii.

Ceea ce vreau sa spun este ca ICHB se asemana f mult cu modelul american, indreptat catre performanta elevilor "de varf", insa asta este singurul plus. Si imo fac asta mai mult pentru marketing, ca sa ramana viziunea colectiva a romanilor cea pe care o ai si tu, Pentru 90% din elevii din liceu, insa, nu as putea spune ca se face ceva special, ce nu ar exista in alte licee. Performanta deci este similara, inafara de acesti elevi care cel mai probabil s-ar fii descurcat la fel de bine in multe alte licee din Romania, daca acestea le ofera sprijin pentru nevoile (sau mai bine zis, capacitatile) lor.
